subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class, model-callable same-session sleep/self-pause primitive, and if so should it be a narrow core tool, part of cron/session-yield semantics, or folded into broader background-continuation design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects agent runtime, gateway wake behavior, session state, user interruption, and config/default policy, so implementation should not proceed without maintainer direction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow sleep primitive
options.body: Design a capped, non-durable self-pause tool that ends the turn and resumes the same session via existing wake/session machinery, with explicit interruption behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader continuation work
options.body: Track this as a use case under the broader post-response/background-continuation design so OpenClaw avoids creating parallel wait and callback contracts.

options.title: Keep current primitives only
options.body: Decline the new tool for now and document cron, process wake, and sessions_yield boundaries as the supported alternatives.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Design a capped, non-durable self-pause tool that ends the turn and resumes the same session via existing wake/session machinery, with explicit interruption behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history spans both cron runtime and agent-core/session behavior, making this the strongest available routing candidate for a cross-boundary product/API decision.
